Commentary.Commentary: We are back. The two umpires have made their way out to the middle as have the players. It will be Will Young and Tom Latham to open the innings for New Zealand. Mitchell Starc will start with the new ball for Australia. Off we go...
... FOURTH INNINGS ...

Right then, the Test is moving at a rapid pace and not many would have seen this collapse coming. Given the effectiveness of Glenn Phillips, Nathan Lyon will be licking his lips at the prospect of bowling on this surface. As for New Zealand, it will be their highest-ever successful Test chase if they get over the line here. Time is not an issue for them but they need to start well and the onus will be on their openers to do that. Back in a bit for the chase.

The man of the moment, Glen Phillips is down for a chat. He says it's a dream come true for him to take a five-fer in home conditions. Adds that Tim Southee is an incredible captain and backs him well along with the support staff. States that their bowlers bowled really well to get this innings bundled up. He further talks about his fifth wicket and how his celebration with the crowd behind him was special. Mentions that they will have to find out a way to combat Nathon Lyon and the pacers but they have enough time to get this chase done.

Australia have been rolled over for 164, giving New Zealand a target of 369 runs to chase. This has been a collapse of epic proportions for Australia. They went into Lunch with a lead of 317 runs and looked on course to go past 400 at the very least with six wickets in hand. However, they capitulated in a really quick time after Lunch, losing their last six wickets for just 37 runs. Once Glenn Phillips broke the partnership between Travis Head and Cameron Green, it all fell apart for the Aussies. Phillips chipped away at the wickets swiftly and did not allow the visitors to string any big partnerships. Matt Henry chipped in as well to pick the last two wickets. Phillips took his maiden first-wicket haul, the first instance of a Kiwi spinner picking five or more wickets at home in 18 years.

The ball gets through the outside edge and rattles the off stump. New Zealand have successfully bundled out the Aussies for 164 runs on the board.

Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for the second session. The two umpires make their way out to the middle followed by the players of New Zealand. They are joined by Cameron Green and Travis Head. Tim Southee will start the proceedings with the ball in this session. Let's play...

As far as New Zealand are concerned, they were in search of early wickets to start the day on a positive note. They were made to wait by the two Aussie batters until Matt Henry saw the back of Lyon just after the half-hour mark. Once they got the breakthrough, the Kiwis were able to tie both ends up and mount the pressure on the batters. Glenn Phillips bowled well in tandem with William O'Rourke, with the former being rewarded for keeping things quiet with the wicket of Khawaja. However, towards the end of the session, New Zealand allowed the Aussie batters to release the pressure, but all in all, it was not a bad session for them. The hosts will look to dry up the boundaries in the afternoon session in their quest to bowl Australia out and not allow them to run away with the game. Join us back at 6.10 am IST (12.40 am GMT) for what promises to be another entertaining session.

SESSION SUMMARY - 100 runs, 27 overs, and 2 wickets. A good session for Australia, one where they lost two wickets but scored at a good clip to be strongly placed in the Test. It was a steady start to the day for them as they resumed their innings with a lead of 217 runs. Having been dropped on the last ball on Day 2, Nathan Lyon continued to ride his luck early on and played his shots to keep the runs flowing. Usman Khawaja was happy to perform the conservative role and held firm at the other end. Lyon fell nine runs short of his maiden Test fifty, resulting in the arrival of the centurion from the first innings, Cameron Green. Khawaja got into his shell and perished in trying to release the pressure. Travis Head had a nervy start to his inning, but the southpaw did well to hang in there and successfully saw through that phase before Lunch with Green. Australia's lead has swelled to 317 runs and with still eight sessions left in the game, they would want to bat for as long as possible.

Commentary.Commentary: We are all in readiness for the action to begin on Day 3! The umpires are out followed by Usman Khawaja and Nathan Lyon who are all set to resume their innings for Australia. The New Zealand fielders take the field and it will be Tim Southee to start the bowling.

New Zealand has endured a series of setbacks, grappling with misfortune across both the days of this Test match. The second day commenced dismally as they struggled to dislodge the final Aussie wicket, allowing their opponents to amass a formidable first-innings total. This setback was compounded by a grim batting performance. Glenn Phillips and Tom Blundell offered some resistance in the middle, along with a brief cameo by Matt Henry as New Zealand's innings was cut short at 179 runs. Despite facing challenges with the bat, New Zealand discovered a ray of hope in their bowling performance in a final burst of eight overs before the end of the day's play. The fierce spell from Tim Southee and Matt Henry claimed two pivotal wickets and created several opportunities injecting a renewed energy into the Kiwi camp which sets the stage for an intriguing battle on Day 3 that is set to unfold in a bit.

Australia enjoyed a stellar start on Day 2, as Cameron Green and Josh Hazlewood forged an impressive 10th wicket partnership, propelling the Aussie score to 383 runs. Buoyed by this strong batting performance, the Australiam bowlers maintained the momentum, dismantling the Kiwi lineup to just 179 runs as they prepared to bat again. Despite their dominance throughout the day, a brief hiccup in the final 30 minutes saw them lose a couple of quick wickets and look tentative with the bat. Although the Aussies are in a commanding position, they will approach Day 3, aiming to further extend their lead and consolidate their grip on the match.

Hello and a warm welcome to the pivotal 'Moving Day' of this enthralling Test match between  New Zealand and Australia! With the Aussies currently holding the advantage, anticipation is high as both teams gear up for what promises to be a thrilling day of cricketing action.
... DAY 3, SESSION 1 ...

With two days of action done and dusted, it is Australia who hold the aces and find themselves in a strong position. The visitors will want to see off that first hour and then drive home the advantage once it gets easier to bat. With plenty of batting still to come, the Aussies would want to bat New Zealand out of the game here. On the other hand, Tim Southee and Co. will be on the hunt for early wickets on the 'Moving Day' as they look to bowl Australia out and keep them to a manageable total. Day 3 will commence at 3.30 am IST (10 pm GMT, the previous day), but you can join us earlier for the build-up. Until then, take care and goodbye!

Glenn Phillips is down for a chat. He says he and Tom Blundell spoke about putting the pressure back onto the bowlers with the pitch offering a lot for the seamers. Adds that Cameron Green and Josh Hazlewood put up a great partnership and took the attack onto them. States that the pitch is still doing a bit and with the crowd behind them it was a good end to the day. Concludes that he will look forward to bowling in those rough marks when he comes on to bowl.

New Zealand would have loved to have another wicket in the day to end the proceedings on a high but it was not to be as Tim Southee dropped a sitter on the last ball. It was an incredibly frustrating start to the day for New Zealand as their plans of bowling Australia out under 300 were thwarted by Cameron Green and Josh Hazlewood's resilient batting. In reply, the hosts were rocked early as they lost Tom Latham in the fifth over before a mix-up in the same over, resulted in a duck for Kane Williamson. It went from bad to worse for New Zealand as they lost three more wickets in the second session. In the third session, Tom Blundell and Glenn Phillips made their intentions clear straight away and were quick to punish loose deliveries. Just as the two batters were starting to find their feet, Tom Blundell was dismissed. Glenn Phillips continued his rescue act but could not bail his side out of trouble and it was the same case with Matt Henry. New Zealand were bowled out for 179, conceding a first-innings lead of 204 runs. With the ball, Tim Southee lead the way late in the day, accounting for two wickets to help his side end the day on a respectable note.

SESSION SUMMARY - 150 runs, 30.1 overs and 7 wickets. An eventful end to a pretty engrossing day of Test cricket! Australia started the day on the front foot and they continue to be in charge of the proceedings at the end of the day. Starting the day with the score of 279, Cameron Green and Josh Hazlewood extended their partnership, heaping further pressure on the hosts. Green, in particular, continued his fine form from the previous day, reaching a remarkable 150 with astute support from Hazlewood. Their stand of 116 runs for the 10th wicket, the highest in Tests against New Zealand, took Australia to 383. The visitors were able to take the momentum into their bowling effort as their pacers put on an absolute clinic of seam bowling. After Tea, they were put under pressure as Glenn Phillips and Tom Blundell looked to counter-attack their way out of trouble. Nathan Lyon was brought in to break the flourishing stand and he did the job by cleaning up the Kiwi lower order. As a result, Australia took a massive first-innings lead of 204 runs. With the bat, it was a shaky start for the visitors, losing Steven Smith and Marnus Labuschagne early. Sent in as the nightwatch man, Nathan Lyon survived a scare on the last ball which meant that Australia went into stumps with only two wickets down and a lead of 217 runs.

Oh dear! THAT'S DROPPED!  Tim Southee drops an easy catch on the last ball of Day 2! Matt Henry bangs it perfectly in the channel on off, making the batter play at it. Nathan Lyon pushes at it away from his body and gets a thick outside edge straight to Tim Southee at second slip. The ball climbs onto him as he moves a bit to his left and it hits him hard on the palm and then onto the grass. That will be STUMPS on Day 2!
